                                          PROJECT NO. 54445

 REVIEW OF PROTOCOLS ADOPTED                          §         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION

 BY THE INDEPENDENT ORGANIZATION                      §                     OF TEXAS


                                          PROJECT NO. 59142

 REVIEW OF ERCOT'S INTERCONNECTION                    §         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 PROCESSES FOR LARGE LOADS
                                                      §                     OF TEXAS



CYRUSONE COMMENTS REGARDING PLANNING GUIDE REVISION REQUEST PGRR145

CyrusOne, LP (“CyrusOne”) respectfully submits its proposed revisions and comments on Planning
Guide Revision Request (“PGRR”) 145 in the above-referenced Public Utility Commission of Texas
(“PUCT”) project numbers 54445 and 59142. CyrusOne appreciates the Electric Reliability Council of
Texas ("ERCOT") and the PUCT's continued efforts to materialize an interconnection queue process for
Interconnecting Large Load Entities ("ILLE"). A significant amount of work has been done to bring
design and implement PGRR145 for Batch Zero at ERCOT. CyrusOne notes that the speed and
breadth of issues addressed by ERCOT and stakeholders in the creation of Batch Zero requirements
meant that there are still some areas that could benefit from greater PUCT clarity. While certain topics
addressed below have been partially addressed by the PUCT, ERCOT, and/or stakeholders, other
topics were not meaningfully explored to understand the full commercial implications.

Given the significant capital at risk for ILLE projects in the Large Load Interconnection Queue
("Queue"), CyrusOne respectfully requests the PUCT to provide further guidance on or before the June
18th Open PUCT Meeting. Clarity on these three areas can mean that real, verifiable projects can
continue to progress without unnecessary ambiguity or hurdles. The PUCT and ERCOT have
expressed their intent to bring real projects forward while reducing speculative loads. Addressing all
recommendations below means non-speculative projects, with billions of dollars of capital at stake,
can continue to progress without delay.

The three areas that the PUCT should make determinations are listed below and justified in these
comments.

    1. Collateral: Provide guidance on under which conditions financial security is refundable and
        what percentage of it shall be refundable

    2. Net Metering Arrangements (“NMA”): Enable NMAs not yet filed with the PUCT to be
        included in Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated

    3. ILLE and Developer Affiliates: Codify an inclusive interpretation of what legal entities can
        qualify under site control, attestations, and long-lead equipment purchases
 INTRODUCTION:

CyrusOne is a leading global data center developer and operator, providing mission-critical
infrastructure for cloud providers, enterprises, and hyperscale customers. Headquartered in Texas,
CyrusOne operates more than 60 data centers worldwide, including a significant presence in Texas.
Across Texas, CyrusOne has over 300 megawatts of data centers capacity currently in operation,
nearly 2 gigawatts of non-duplicative data center capacity under construction.

Our operations rely on dependable, robust, and economical electricity to support high-density
computing environments that enable digital transformation across industries. Our facilities serve over
1,000 customers, including approximately 200 Fortune 1000 companies, CyrusOne’s leading global
platform of hybrid-cloud and multi-cloud deployments offers customers colocation, hyperscale and
build-to-suit environments, which help enhance the strategic connections of their essential data
infrastructures and support the achievement of sustainability goals. CyrusOne data centers offer
world-class flexibility, enabling clients to modernize, simplify and rapidly respond to changing
demands. Combining exceptional financial strength, a broad global footprint and continued investment
in key digital gateway markets, CyrusOne provides the world’s largest companies with long-term
stability and strategic advantages at scale.

ISSUE 1: COLLATERAL

Overview:

The PUCT and ERCOT have refined their view on large load interconnections under PGRR145,
CyrusOne has been supportive of the implementation of development requirements, including
financial commitments, to help screen which projects within the Queue are likely to progress from
concept to development to execution. PGRR145 has established varying levels of financial security
commitment based on the criteria in which a project is included in Batch Zero.

While PGRR145 outlines the amount of financial security required, additional clarity needed from the
PUCT is critical.

During its June 11th, 2026, Batch Readiness Meeting, ERCOT flagged that in a recently published FAQ
on Batch Zero, that PGRR145 does not address refundability of financial security. ERCOT
recommended that parties refer to the ongoing proceedings at the PUCT, including Project Nos.
58481, Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards Under PURA § 37.0561, and
59142, Review of ERCOT's Interconnection Processes for Large Loads.

CyrusOne is progressing several projects through Batch Zero, but there are two key issues we have
encountered that are tied to refundability of financial security required of PGRR145.

ERCOT has established a deadline to submit required Batch Zero eligibility materials to its TDSP,
including applicable security by July 10th. July 10th, 2026, is also the same day that ERCOT has
established as its deadline to review and approve studies. One or more TDSPs have communicated
that they are requiring eligibility materials, including applicable security by June 26 th, 2026. This timing
creates a critical issue for any project that does not yet know if it is included in Batch Zero or Batch
One.

An ILLE and their respective financial institution posting financial security may take up to two weeks to
prepare, review, and post applicable financial security for projects in the tens to hundreds of millions of
dollars to the interconnecting TDSP. If an ILLE is required to post financial security by either of those
timelines, they need to know from ERCOT and their interconnecting TDSP at least two weeks in
 advance whether they are included in Batch Zero or not. A financial institution and the ILLE may not
wish to or be able to post financial security without knowing if a project is included in Batch Zero.

Where this issue becomes even more concerning for ILLEs and their financial institutions is the
ambiguity on how financial security will be treated by the TDSP and ERCOT if a project posts financial
security and later finds out it is not eligible for Batch Zero inclusion. If an ILLE can post tens to
hundreds of millions of dollars of financial security, it should be refunded 100% such that it can be
reallocated to projects, instead of being held by the TDSP or ERCOT.

As CyrusOne has worked to finalize its documentation on projects, it has encountered differing
perspectives on how financial security (collateral and CIAC) will be managed and refunded. These
requirements also need to be clarified soon as TDSPs and ILLEs work to finalize agreements which
include financial security requirements.

The PUCT and ERCOT should establish clarity on refundability of financial security to ensure
consistent implementation across ERCOT.

Proposed PUCT Recommendations for Collateral:

CyrusOne respectfully requests the PUCT provide clear guidance on the following:

    1.
         When required by PGRR145, ILLEs can post financial security (collateral and CIAC) for Batch
         Zero Base Load and Batch Zero to be Studied & Allocated up until July 22nd, 2026 for inclusion
         in Batch Zero, instead of July 10th, 2026.

    2. 100% of financial security (collateral and CIAC) posted for a project believed to be included in
         Batch Zero, but later determined to be Batch One, be returned to the ILLE.

    3. ILLE’s that qualify as Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated should be eligible for a 100%
         refund of their financial security (collateral and CIAC) if they rescind the project, if after they’ve
         been notified by ERCOT their MW allocation, the project is no longer viable.

    4. ILLE’s that qualify as Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated should be eligible for a 100%
         refund of their financial security (collateral and CIAC) that applies to the difference between
         what was initially requested and what was allocated by ERCOT.

    5. Establish a timeline for when and how a TDSP must refund Batch Zero financial security.

ISSUE 2: NET METERING ARRANGEMENTS

Overview:

Certain projects are structured to comply with Texas Senate Bill 6 (“SB 6”) through Net-Metering
Arrangements (“NMA”) that allow existing generators to continue supporting grid reliability during
emergency conditions, subject to approval by the PUCT. These projects require ERCOT reliability
assessments and PUCT approval to energize. Following the passage of SB 6, CyrusOne made
good‑faith investment decisions—including securing institutional capital, long‑lead equipment,
generator agreements, tenant commitments tied to energization timelines, and site control—based on
the framework the Legislature established.

The PUCT ordered that NMAs filed with the Commission by March 4, 2026, may be eligible for
inclusion in Batch Zero Base Load. ERCOT has codified this position in PGRR145. Given this
established date, an open question remains as to whether NMAs filed after March 4, 2026, may
qualify for inclusion in Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated.
 Absent the proposed refinement below, certain projects may lack a viable near-term study pathway.
For example, a known 2028 NMA under § 39.169 that is not designated as baseload and did not
submit a Commission application by March 4, 2026, would be effectively precluded from participation
in Batch Zero. At the same time, the legacy LLIS process is expected to be unavailable, and Batch Zero
access would remain limited to projects that independently satisfy the criteria set forth in § 9.2.1.2. As
a result, such projects would likely be deferred to Batch One, creating a material risk that in-service
timelines for 2028 projects slip to 2029 or later.

As illuminated by Vistra in their comments, the number, size, and scale of projects that could fit into
Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated, may be less than 5% of the total Large Load Queue.
Meanwhile, these projects have little to no transmission upgrades, significant investor-grade entities
advancing these large loads, and provide little to no transmission reliability impact.

CyrusOne shared in its comments1 to ERCOT that these NMA projects should not be subject to
ERCOT Batching delays and that inclusion of these projects in Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated
should be added to PGRR145, CyrusOne is supportive of Vistra's2 initial proposed concept that the
inclusion of NMAs with an initial energization date between January 1, 2028, and December 31, 2028,
to be included in Batch Zero to be Studied and Allocated, even if they don’t have completed studies.
Various parties have expressed their support for addressing this critical gap in projects that are already
in flight but now may be subjected to delays as they are forced to be included in Batch 1. This concern
was highlighted by the Data Center Coalition3, BKV4, and Luminary Strategies5. This approach would
minimize delays for 39.169 NMAs with a 2028 energization target and enable in-flight NMA projects
to proceed consistent with their development timelines.

Proposed PUCT Recommendations for Net Metering Arrangements:

CyrusOne respectfully requests the PUCT provide clear guidance on the treatment of NMAs that were
not filed by the March deadline for inclusion in Batch Zero. As recommended by Vistra and supported
by other parties noted above:

    1. Add language to Section 9.2.1.2(2) to enable 39.169 NMAs with an assigned LLI# and initial
        energization date between January 1, 2028, and December 31, 2028, and not already
        included in base load to be included in Batch Zero as load to be studied and allocated in Batch
        Zero: The goal is to bring NMAs that ERCOT is already aware of into Batch Zero, preventing
        future delays to 39.169 NMAs with a 2028 initial energization date.

ISSUE 3: AFFILIATES

Overview:

As drafted, PGRR145 requires an attestation from the ILLE that it holds one or more qualifying
property interests sufficient to demonstrate site control for purposes of Batch Zero eligibility.

 PGRR145 further requires the interconnecting TDSP to notify ERCOT that the ILLE has attested that
all equipment with lead times of at least 18 months has been ordered. This framework introduces
ambiguity as to whether the ILLE itself must be the entity that directly procures such equipment or
demonstrates site control itself, or whether procurement by another party, such as an affiliated entity,
tenant, or end-use customer, is sufficient to satisfy the requirement.

At the most recent Batch Readiness Workshop 6, ERCOT indicated that the ILLE must hold the relevant
real property interests in its own legal name and that ownership by an affiliate does not satisfy the
requirements of PGRR145. This interpretation is inconsistent with typical project development and
financing structures and creates significant practical challenges. Many projects rely on commonly used
arrangements in which property ownership, development, and operational control are distributed
among affiliated entities for financing, tax, and risk management purposes. Requiring the ILLE to
directly hold title to the property may therefore impede otherwise viable projects from meeting the
July 10 compliance deadline.

From a transactional perspective, it is standard practice for affiliated entities to hold title to discrete
parcels or individual facilities within a larger data center campus. A single site may consist of multiple
buildings leased to different tenants, each supported by separate financing structures tied to specific
facilities and associated large load interconnection points. These arrangements are foundational to
how large-scale data center developments are structured and financed.

Accordingly, CyrusOne respectfully requests that the Commission provide clarifying guidance that
allows for a more flexible and commercially reasonable interpretation of PGRR145. Specifically, the
Commission should confirm that site control and equipment procurement requirements may be
satisfied through affiliated entities, tenants, or other project participants, so long as the ILLE can
demonstrate sufficient control over the site and project readiness in a manner consistent with the
intent of the rule.

Proposed Recommendations for Affiliates:

    1. As recommended by TIEC 7 and supported by Crusoe8, confirm that PGRR145's site control
         requirement may be satisfied where the ILLE provides documentary evidence demonstrating
         an enforceable legal right to use, develop, occupy, lease, acquire, construct on, or otherwise
         control the relevant site for the planned large load facilities.

    2. Confirm that the PGRR145’s long lead-time equipment requirements may be satisfied where
         the ILLE provides documentary evidence demonstrating an enforceable legal right to use,
         develop, occupy, lease, acquire, construct on, or otherwise control the relevant site for the
         planned large load facilities.

 SUMMARY:

CyrusOne appreciates the opportunity to submit our perspective into the record. We look forward to
working collaboratively with the PUCT and ERCOT and appreciate any opportunity for increased
transparency and dialogue among these parties.

 PGRR145 further requires the interconnecting TDSPto notify ERCOT that the ILLE has attested that
all equipment with lead times of at least 18 months has been ordered. This framework introduces
ambiguity as to whether the ILLE itself must be the entity that directly procures such equipment or
demonstrates site control itself, or whether procurement by another party, such as an affiliated entity,
tenant, or end-use customer, is sufficient to satisfythe requirement.

At the most recent Batch Readiness Workshopt ERCOT indicated that the ILLE must hold the relevant
real property interests in its own legal name and that ownership by an affiliate does not satisfy the
requirements of PGRR145. This interpretation is inconsistent with typical project development and
financing structures and creates significant practical challenges. Many projects rely on commonly used
arrangements in which property ownership, development, and operational control are distributed
among affiliated entities for financing, tax, and risk management purposes. Requiring the ILLE to
directly hold title to the property may therefore impede otherwise viable projects from meeting the
July 10 compliance deadline.

From a transactional perspective, it is standard practice for affiliated entities to hold title to discrete
parcels or individual facilities within a larger data center campus. A single site may consist of multiple
buildings leased to different tenants, each supported by separate financing structures tied to specific
facilities and associated large load interconnection points. These arrangements are foundational to
how large-scale data center developments are structured and financed.

Accordingly, CyrusOne respectfully requests that the Commission provide clarifying guidance that
allows for a more flexible and commercially reasonable interpretation of PGRR145. Specifically, the
Commission should confirm that site control and equipment procurement requirements may be
satisfied through affiliated entities, tenants, or other project participants, so long as the ILLE can
demonstrate sufficient control over the site and project readiness in a manner consistent with the
intent of the rule.

Proposed Recommendations for Affiliates:

    1.   As recommended by TIEC7 and supported by Crusoe8, confirm that PGRR145's site control
         requirement may be satisfied where the ILLE provides documentary evidence demonstrating
         an enforceable legal right to use, develop, occupy, lease, acquire, construct on, or otherwise
         control the relevant site for the planned large load facilities.

    2.   Confirm that the PGRR145's long lead-time equipment requirements may be satisfied where
         the ILLE provides documentary evidence demonstrating an enforceable legal rightto use,
         develop, occupy, lease, acquire, construct on, or otherwise control the relevant site for the
         planned large load facilities.
